stage1_assessment: The four previously recorded PR #3 schema counterexamples are repaired in the updated branch by source inspection. The cases below are not claims that isolated JSON Schema should solve repository-level referential integrity; they freeze the next continuity oracles so Stage 2 identity and later state/runtime validation cannot silently invent hidden reference semantics.

cases.observed_contract_fact: evidence-record.subject_ref and artifact.evidence_refs are unconstrained non-empty strings, while artifact identity and version are separate fields.
cases.scenario: Artifact artifact.rules exists at version 2, but an automated_tested evidence record was produced for version 1. The artifact at version 2 references that evidence id. Each object can remain shape-valid even though the evidence does not establish the current artifact version.

evidence.claim: Tests passed for the rules artifact.

cases.required_oracle: Evidence used to support an artifact state must resolve to the exact artifact version/content identity it tested, or to an equivalent immutable subject reference. A later artifact version must not inherit earlier strong evidence merely because a stable artifact id matches.
cases.recommended_layer: Stage 2 identity/reference semantics plus cross-object validation; do not rely on an undocumented string convention.

cases.observed_contract_fact: return packets and artifact provenance record a base_state_revision, but isolated schema validation cannot compare those bases with the current canonical revision or with the version of a targeted artifact/dependency.
cases.scenario: A return packet produced from revision.fixture.0001 modifies artifact.rules. Revision.fixture.0002 already changed artifact.rules before this packet reaches integration. The packet remains shape-valid and its artifact can also remain shape-valid.
cases.required_oracle: Integration must detect that the packet's target/dependency state has advanced from its declared base and reject, defer, or request an explicit repair/rebase. A stale packet must never silently apply to a newer artifact version.
cases.recommended_layer: Stage 3/4 state-store and work-ledger validation, with the invariant named before implementation.

cases.observed_contract_fact: epoch.base_state_revision and return-packet.base_state_revision are explicit, but the epoch schema cannot require every referenced packet to use the epoch base or define sequential/hybrid progression across packet bases.
cases.scenario: A sealed parallel epoch declares base revision.fixture.0001 and references packet.a plus packet.b. packet.a was produced from revision.fixture.0001, while packet.b was produced from revision.fixture.0002. All three objects can be individually shape-valid.
cases.required_oracle: For a parallel epoch, every included packet must be demonstrably bound to the epoch base. Sequential/hybrid execution must record enough explicit progression/order semantics to replay why a packet used a later base rather than inferring this from array order or private occupant memory.
cases.recommended_layer: Cross-object epoch validator before the parallel-vs-sequential experiment is treated as measured evidence.

cases.observed_contract_fact: artifact.supersedes_ref is an optional non-empty string with no cross-object acyclicity or self-reference constraint.
cases.scenario: artifact.rules version 2 declares supersedes_ref = artifact.rules, or two stored artifact versions form a supersession cycle. Individual artifact objects can be shape-valid while lineage becomes non-reconstructable.
cases.required_oracle: Artifact supersession must resolve to a prior immutable artifact version and must be acyclic. Self-supersession, forward references, and cycles must fail loudly rather than producing plausible but false provenance.
cases.recommended_layer: Stage 2 immutable identity plus Stage 3 repository-level referential validation.
